answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce token stake before it can submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud or duplicate identities. A Sybil attacker must fund every persona, so multiplying accounts raises the capital at risk rather than merely multiplying free votes; passing as cedar, sable, or harbor does not evade the shared collateral rule. The cost is not just acquiring tokens, but leaving them illiquid and exposed to loss while honest agents can build reputation over time.
